title: Exponential and logistic growth
caption: With unlimited resources a population grows exponentially, a J-shaped curve. In a real environment growth slows as the population nears the carrying capacity K, giving an S-shaped logistic curve. Growth is fastest when the population is K/2.
alt: Two curves of population size against time: a J-shaped exponential curve that climbs off the top of the graph, and an S-shaped logistic curve that rises fastest at half the carrying capacity of 1,000 and levels off at 1,000.
description: Exponential growth (unlimited resources): a J-shaped curve that keeps accelerating.
Logistic growth: slows as resources run short and levels off at the carrying capacity K = 1,000.
The logistic curve rises fastest when the population is K/2 = 500, at about 9 time units.
Carrying capacity is the maximum population the environment can support.
